How the score works (0–100; it only ranks cars that already pass every rule)
  • 25 pts · Price: full points at $30,000 or less, none at $40,000
  • 21 pts · Plug-in hybrid or electric: all or nothing
  • 10 pts · Gas mileage: none at 20 mpg, full at 40 mpg
  • 10 pts · Premium sound system (Harman Kardon, B&O, Burmester…)
  • 8 pts · All-wheel drive (not shown: 30%)
  • 7 pts · Black interior (brown / saddle are allowed but get none; not shown: 30%)
  • 5 pts · Spare tire (not shown: 40%)
  • 4 pts · Real leather seats (not shown on the listing: 40%)
  • 4 pts · Cooled seats (not shown: 40%)
  • 4 pts · Ground clearance of 8 inches or more

Each item gives its points in full, in part or not at all, and the score adds them up. A car only reaches 100 if it is best on everything at once, so even very good matches usually land between 50 and 75.

    Cars that were on this dashboard and later disappeared from the dealer's site (sold or taken down). The link may no longer work.

    Cars you sent in from dealers the search can't read. The search can't tell when these sell, so check them now and then: tap the car to open the dealer's page, then tap Still available, Update price (if it changed) or No longer available. Checks older than a week turn yellow as a reminder. A car you mark no longer available moves to the Sold tab at once (the next search makes it permanent).

    Dealers the search couldn't read by any method, so their cars may be missing from this page. Tap a model to open that dealer's own certified inventory for it (or All certified inventory). Have a look, then tap Mark checked. Checks older than a week turn yellow as a reminder. Dealers covered by a brand-wide certified search aren't listed.

    What each trim includes, by model year, for every model your search looks for. Trims marked not on your list are shown so you can compare. Researched from the manufacturers' own press sites and brochures; dealers can add options, so check the window sticker.

    Warranties by brand (new-car and certified pre-owned)

    Each car on the Available tab also shows the coverage it has left and when each part is expected to end. How the end date is estimated: most warranties count from the day the car was first sold new (its "in-service date"). Listings don't show that, so it's assumed to be about April of the model year (a car can be up to ~9 months either side; ask the dealer for the exact date). A warranty also ends when the car reaches its mileage limit; that date assumes you drive about 12,000 miles a year. The earlier of the two is shown.

    Price = advertised price + dealer fees (estimated when the page didn't list them), before tax. Monthly = $8,000 down, 60 months at 5.34%, 9.75% tax, $400 gov't fees. MPG = combined (city/hwy below); "EPA" means the listing didn't show it, so it's the official rating from fueleconomy.gov; plug-in hybrids show gas-only MPG.
